title: Passage to the algebraic closure of a separably closed field
statement:
Let $k$ be a separably closed field with algebraic closure $\bar k$, let $C$
be a $k$-scheme, $u:C_{\bar k}\to C$ the projection, and $F$ an abelian sheaf
on $C_{\mathrm{ét}}$. Then $u$ is a universal homeomorphism and the pullback
maps

$$
H^q(C_{\mathrm{ét}},F)\longrightarrow H^q((C_{\bar k})_{\mathrm{ét}},u^{-1}F)
$$

are isomorphisms for all $q$. If $k\subseteq k'$ is a further separably
closed field and $\bar k\subseteq\bar k'$ are compatible algebraic closures,
then the square of pullback maps formed by $C_{\bar k'}\to C_{\bar k}\to C$
and $C_{\bar k'}\to C_{k'}\to C$ commutes.

proof.text: If $k$ has characteristic zero [def-pc-separably-closed], every $\alpha\in\bar k$ has an irreducible minimal polynomial over $k$, which is separable in characteristic zero and hence has a root in $k$; so it has degree one, $\alpha\in k$, and $\bar k=k$, which is purely inseparable over $k$ by the characteristic-zero clause of [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. If $k$ has characteristic $p>0$, the existing purely-inseparable-closure result [lem-pc-kbar-pure-insep] gives that $\bar k/k$ is purely inseparable. In either case, apply [lem-pc-spec-pure-insep-integral-radicial-surjective] to $\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and then [lem-pc-integral-radicial-surjective-universal-homeomorphism] to obtain a universal homeomorphism. By the base-change definition [def-pc-base-change], $u:C_{\bar k}=C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\to C$ is its base change; [lem-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-base-change] therefore makes $u$ a universal homeomorphism. Applying [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance] gives the equivalence of étale topoi and the cohomology isomorphisms $H^q(C,F)\to H^q(C_{\bar k},u^{-1}F)$ for every $q$.

For the square, compatibility of the algebraic-closure inclusions makes the two composites $C_{\bar k'}\to C$ equal: one factors through $C_{\bar k}$ and the other through $C_{k'}$. Clause 4 (composition) of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] identifies the pullback along either composite with the corresponding composite of pullback maps, using the canonical inverse-image composition isomorphism. Thus the two paths in the displayed cohomology square agree in every degree.
